cards.title: Slow breathing
cards.why: A slow out-breath helps the body settle when it feels wound up.
steps: Sit comfortably and let your shoulders drop.
Breathe in gently through your nose for a count of four.
Breathe out slowly through your mouth for a count of six.
Repeat for about five rounds, then notice how your body feels.
cards.tip: Try it at the same time each day, such as after brushing your teeth.

cards.title: Five senses grounding
cards.why: Noticing the room around you brings attention back to the present moment.
steps: Name 5 things you can see.
Name 4 things you can touch or feel.
Name 3 things you can hear.
Name 2 things you can smell, and 1 thing you can taste.
Take one slow breath and look around once more.

cards.title: Worry time
cards.why: Giving worries a set time can stop them from following you all day.
steps: Pick a 10 minute slot each day and keep it the same.
When a worry shows up earlier, jot a few words and tell yourself 'later, at worry time'.
At worry time, read the list and ask which worries you can act on.
Pick one small action for a worry you can act on, and let the rest go for today.

cards.title: Thought check
cards.why: Looking at a hard thought from a few sides can make it feel less fixed.
steps: Write the thought that is bothering you in one sentence.
Ask: what is the evidence for it, and what is the evidence against it?
Ask: what would I say to a close friend who had this thought?
Write a kinder, more balanced version of the thought.

cards.title: One small step
cards.why: Starting with a very small task makes it easier to get moving when energy is low.
steps: Choose one task you have been putting off.
Shrink it until it takes five minutes or less.
Set a timer for five minutes and start.
When the timer ends, you may stop or carry on. Either is fine.
Notice how it felt to begin.

cards.title: Evening wind-down
cards.why: A steady, calm routine before bed helps the mind and body get ready for sleep.
steps: Pick a regular time to start winding down each evening.
Put screens away about thirty minutes before bed.
Dim the lights and do something quiet, such as reading or gentle stretching.
Go to bed and get up at about the same times each day.
cards.tip: If your mind is busy, write tomorrow's tasks on paper first.

cards.title: Three good things
cards.why: Noticing small good moments helps balance the mind's habit of focusing on problems.
steps: Before bed, write down three things that went okay today. Small things count.
Next to each, write why it happened or what part you played.
Read them once, then put the page away.

cards.title: Reach out
cards.why: Small moments of connection can ease loneliness and stress.
steps: Think of one person you feel at ease with.
Send a short message or call, even just to say hello.
If it feels hard, plan a time and place to do it this week.

cards.title: Gentle movement
cards.why: Light movement can lift energy and mood without needing a full workout.
steps: Choose a gentle activity you can do today, such as a short walk or stretching.
Start with ten minutes and go at an easy pace.
Notice how your body and mood feel afterwards.
cards.tip: Check with your doctor first if you have a health condition or injury.
